messages:
maya: FYI pushed a tiny helm patch to payments chart to wire ExternalSecret for stripe API key. Wanted a quick sanity check on the namespace mapping — we saw a secret appear in the wrong ns in staging earlier.
sam: which chart/values? link?
maya: chart: charts/payments, values override under values/externalsecret.yaml. Patch uses a hook to create a ExternalSecret in the release namespace, but the ExternalSecrets controller is resolving the vault path using `{{ .Release.Namespace }}` in the template and then writing to a different ns for some pods. weird. PR: https://git/repo/pulls/1421
leo: can you paste the hook/template snippet here?
maya: sure — this is the hook we added: 
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: bootstrap-secrets
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: create-es
          image: bitnami/kubectl:1.26
          command: ["sh","-c","kubectl apply -f /manifests/externalsecret.yaml -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}"]
---
# externalsecret.yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: stripe-key
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1m
  secretStoreRef:
    name: vault-store
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
  target:
    name: stripe-key
    template:
      metadata:
        labels:
          app: payments
  data:
    - secretKey: api_key
      remoteRef:
        key: secret/data/stripe/{{ .Release.Name }}/api_key
```
maya: observed: in staging the ClusterSecretStore side wrote a Secret into "platform" ns for some reason. infra-bot reported: "external-secrets controller mapped target namespace to 'platform' because target.template.metadata.namespace was empty"
infra-bot: incident detected: externalsecret stripe-key created secret in namespace=platform, expected=payments. created_by_job=bootstrap-secrets. controller=external-secrets v1.7.2.
sam: I think ExternalSecrets v1.x will fallback to the controller ns if target.template.metadata.namespace is omitted. In our cluster, the controller runs in 'platform' so that matches the symptom.
leo: yes — target.template.metadata.namespace is different from ExternalSecret.metadata.namespace. If you set target.namespace explicitly it will be used. The helm template currently sets metadata.namespace only at top-level.
ben: quick fix: add target.namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }} under spec.target in the externalsecret manifest. That forces the Secret to be created there. Also remove the post-install job; helm can render the resource directly (unless ordering was required).
maya: hmm we used the job because the secret store didn't exist in earlier boots, that was the reason. But adding target.namespace is low-risk. I'll patch and test.
sam: for long-term, prefer rendering ExternalSecret as a normal manifest in the chart and rely on Helm's hooks only for ordering when unavoidable. Jobs are flaky for idempotency.
leo: another angle: the ClusterSecretStore uses role bindings to allow cross-ns writes; we should audit that to ensure no writes outside release namespaces. Might be fine but worth checking.
maya: patch pushed to PR 1421 with target.namespace added and removed the job. Ran `kubectl apply -f` in staging and verified the secret lands in payments ns.
ben: can you also add a Terraform policy note? our infra-iam repo has a policy that ClusterSecretStore should not have wildcard write perms. Add a note to the PR description so infra-iam owners can triage.
maya: done — added note: "please verify ClusterSecretStore RBAC for vault-store; prefer least-priv write scope".
leo: Thanks — would you also include a smoke test command snippet in the PR description? e.g. `kubectl -n payments get secret stripe-key -o yaml | grep api_key`
maya: added smoke test and a short k8s diff output. tagging @ben for a quick review on the RBAC comment.
ben: taking a look now, should be quick. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — will merge once ben approves, then we'll schedule a 2-step deploy to prod after infra-iam check.
infra-bot: deploy-checker: pre-flight OK for chart payments v1.3.7-rc2, no breaking schema changes detected.
